screening.reason: Inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE resting-state fMRI data explicitly and reports a diagnostic prediction (ASD vs TC classification) analysis.

evidence_spans.text: It compiles a dataset of 1112 R-fMRI par- ticipants by gathering data from 17 diﬀerent sites. Af- ter preprocessing, we selected 871 to meet quality criteria for MRI and phenotypic information.
evidence_spans.claim: The analysed cohort is 871 of 1112 ABIDE I participants from 17 sites, selected after a quality-control step.

evidence_spans.text: all participants (871 individuals, 727 males and 144 fe- males, 6 to 64 years old) is the full set of individuals that passed QA
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort demographics for the full analysed subsample (871 individuals, 727 male / 144 female, ages 6-64).

evidence_spans.text: Data were selected based on the results of quality visual in- spection by three human experts
evidence_spans.claim: QC rule was expert visual inspection of preprocessed data rather than a numeric motion threshold.

evidence_spans.text: We speciﬁcally used the data processed with the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes [34] (C-PAC).
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing pipeline used was C-PAC via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project.

evidence_spans.text: Note that the ROI were all deﬁned on the training set to avoid possible overﬁtting.
evidence_spans.claim: Atlas/ROI estimation was confined to the training fold, an explicit leakage-control measure.

evidence_spans.text: This validation with a leave-one- site-out cross-validation strategy reduces the risk of over- ﬁtting data from a single site
For inter-site prediction, the highest accuracy obtained on the whole dataset is 66.8% (see Table 2) which ex- ceeds previously published ABIDE ﬁndings [53, 13, 54] and chance at 53.7%
evidence_spans.claim: Best inter-site (leave-site-out) classification accuracy on the full 871-subject ABIDE sample was 66.8%, above chance (53.7%).

evidence_spans.text: the best predicting pipeline is MSDL, tangent space embedding and l2-regularized classi- ﬁers (SVC-l2 and ridge classiﬁer)
evidence_spans.claim: Best-performing pipeline combination: MSDL atlas, tangent-space connectivity embedding, l2-regularized classifiers.

assessments.support: 871 of 1112 ABIDE I participants from 17 sites retained after QA; demographics (sex, age range) and per-site/per-subsample N reported in Table A2.

Multiple atlas/parcellation and connectivity-estimation options systematically compared and reported (Harvard-Oxford, Yeo, ICA, MSDL, K-Means, Ward; correlation, partial correlation, tangent embedding).

Paper states diagnosis vs typical control (TC) status was used but does not specify the diagnostic instrument/criteria underlying ABIDE's phenotypic label beyond noting diagnostic/assessment protocols vary across sites.
ROIs defined on the training set only, hyperparameters tuned via nested cross-validation, and primary evaluation used leave-one-site-out CV rather than pooled random splits.

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-controlled predictive ABIDE I study with explicit leakage control (training-set-only atlas estimation, nested CV) and site-aware evaluation (leave-one-site-out); main uncertainty is the unspecified diagnostic-label source.

charting.title: Deriving reproducible biomarkers from multi-site resting-state data: An Autism-based example
charting.authors: Abraham A; Milham M; Di Martino A; Craddock RC; Samaras D; Thirion B; Varoquaux G
charting.dataset_openly_available: Precomputed MSDL atlas released at a project URL (MSDL_ABIDE.zip); built on the publicly available Preprocessed Connectomes Project C-PAC release
charting.specific_features: Connectome edge weights; atlases compared: Harvard-Oxford, Yeo, ICA, MSDL, K-Means, Ward; connectivity measures: correlation, partial correlation, tangent embedding
charting.feature_extraction_tools: Preprocessed Connectomes Project C-PAC; Nilearn, scikit-learn 0.17.1
charting.top_features_identified: Default Mode Network, pareto-insular network, and semantic ROI connections distinguishing ASD from TC
charting.validation_methodology: Leave-one-site-out cross-validation (inter-site) and intra-site cross-validation, with nested cross-validation for hyperparameter selection; ROI/atlas estimation confined to the training set
charting.key_performance_results: Best inter-site accuracy 66.8% (chance 53.7%) on the full 871-subject sample using MSDL + tangent embedding + l2-regularized classifier; abstract reports 67% prediction accuracy, exceeding previously published ABIDE results (60%)
charting.summary_key_findings: A systematic comparison of ABIDE R-fMRI pipeline choices (atlas, connectivity measure, classifier) shows MSDL + tangent-space embedding + l2-regularized classifiers give the best inter-site prediction accuracy (66.8%, full 871-subject sample), with accuracy improving as more training subjects are included.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 871 of 1112 participants (403 ASD, 468 TC) from 17 sites, after QA; subsamples of varying homogeneity also analysed (e.g. 736, 639, 420, 226 participants)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed ABIDE I data; systematic comparison of 6 atlas/parcellation methods x 3 connectivity measures x classifiers (SVC, ridge); leave-one-site-out and intra-site cross-validation with nested CV for hyperparameters and training-set-only ROI estimation
narrative_row.outcomes: Best inter-site accuracy 66.8% (chance 53.7%) with MSDL atlas, tangent-space embedding, l2-regularized classifiers; accuracy increases with training sample size; discriminative connections implicate Default Mode Network, pareto-insular and semantic ROI networks
narrative_row.key_limitations: Diagnostic label source/criteria not detailed; heterogeneous site protocols; computationally very costly pipeline comparison (reported ~10 CPU-years without grid parallelization)
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Methodological benchmark paper establishing which PCP/C-PAC pipeline + atlas + classifier choices work best on the full ABIDE I release, directly informing which pipeline/atlas combinations recur in later ABIDE classification work
